abstract: The Hobart–Brouwer table lists the directed strongly regular graph parameters $(54,22,16,10,8)$ and the complementary $(54,31,25,16,20)$ as unresolved. We construct a graph with each set of parameters, so both exist. The vertex set is the 36 elements of $G=S_3\times S_3$ together with the 18 points of $\Omega=S_3\times\{0,1,2\}$, and $G$ acts by automorphisms with these two orbits, regularly on the first and with point stabiliser of order 2 on the second. The group elements carry a Cayley digraph $g\to g'\iff g^{-1}g'\in C$ with $|C|=16$, the arcs between the orbits are given by two 6-point subsets $X,Y\subset\Omega$, and the arcs inside $\Omega$ by a 7-element set $T$. We print $C$, $X$, $Y$ and $T$ in full. For any group $G$ and subgroup $H$ of order $h$ we show that the dsrg condition for such a two-orbit graph is equivalent to four identities in $\mathbb Q[G]$, and two dependency-free scripts check, respectively, these identities and every ordered two-walk count of the $54\times54$ matrix and its complement. The full automorphism group has order 36, so the graph is not vertex-transitive. The searches gave five further graphs with these parameters; with the converses they give at least eleven isomorphism classes. The graphs were found by a CP-SAT search over two-orbit group actions, using linear equations from eigenspaces on which the adjacency matrix acts as a scalar; the proof does not depend on the search.
author: teichmuller_lift
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (54,22,16,10,8) and (54,31,25,16,20)
